messages:
marta: heads up — our playbook auto-escalation is firing for a bunch of accounts that actually never completed onboarding. looks like a mapping bug between Contact.role and Onboard.owner. seeing false positives in the renewal-risk dashboard. :wave:

sana: ugh. saw a couple of those earlier when i was spot-checking. the contact join is using `primary_contact` instead of `owner_email` in the healthscore ETL — so accounts with handoffs get flagged.

alex: can we add a guardrail before escalation? minimal check: `last_onboard_event_at IS NOT NULL AND onboarding_progress >= 0.7` — prevents mid-onboard churn from being treated as churned. also we should gate the escalation with recent_activity > 14d.

liam: for historical flags we need a migration plan. do we want to reprocess 90 days of events or just patch the playbook rules and let new signals win? reprocessing could be expensive.

marta: good q. i'd prefer a staged approach: patch playbook to stop new false positives, then run a small backfill for enterprise accounts only. open to alternatives.

sana: i'll draft the playbook condition and run a dry-run against prod-sample this afternoon. quick SQL i'm testing:```sql
SELECT a.account_id, a.healthscore, c.role, o.progress, o.last_event_at
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN contacts c ON c.account_id = a.account_id AND c.is_primary = true
LEFT JOIN onboarding_status o ON o.account_id = a.account_id
WHERE a.healthscore < 50 AND (o.progress IS NULL OR o.progress < 0.7) -- candidates that should NOT escalate
LIMIT 200;
```

marta: nice. can you also output contact.email + contact.role? some of the false positives were because a partner contact was marked primary.

sana: yup, will include `c.email, c.role`. also adding this quick playbook snippet to require `onboarding.completed = false` before escalation.```yaml
when:
  - condition: account.healthscore < 40
  - condition: onboarding.progress >= 0.7
actions:
  - escalate: account.owner
  - notify: cs-queue
  - set_tag: "escalated_auto"
```

alex: nit: add `and recent_activity_days <= 90` to the first condition. otherwise stale accounts slip through.

liam: for backfill plan: we can run the reprocess as a batched job by org tier. propose: week1 = enterprise, week2 = mid-market, week3 = long-tail. each batch writes to `account_flags.backfill_run_<date>` so we can revert. cost estimate ~ 12 GPU-hours for full enterprise run (mostly ETL CPU work).

marta: sounds reasonable. timeline? our weekly release window is Tue 03:00 UTC. i'd like patch + dry-run Mon, canary Tue, full enable Wed.

cs-bot: ALERT: high rate of "escalated_auto" tags created in last 30m (125 events). channel:#customer-success. source: playbook-engine.

marta: saw that. i'm pausing the rule temporarily to stop noise. please do not touch the backfill until i confirm. @sana @alex

sana: paused. running the dry-run now against a copy of prod (no writes). i'll share the sample CSV for review: `account_id,owner_email,primary_contact_email,contact_role,onboarding_progress,healthscore,recent_activity_days`

alex: when you share results drop 5-10 obvious FP cases. i'll validate owners and then we can run canary.

liam: tagging ops to watch release concurrency. also suggest adding a short TTL on auto tags (`auto_escalated_expires_at`) so if the flag was wrong it naturally falls off.

marta: good call. add TTL of 14 days for auto-escalations. if owner reopens, we'll persist manual tags.

sana: will run dry-run and post subset CSV and the raw query results in #customer-success in ~2h. i'm also attaching the filter we use in the renewal-risk dashboard to cross-check: `where tag = 'escalated_auto' and created_at > now() - interval '30 days'`.

marta: thanks. i'll own rollout and comms to AMs. planning email template for affected owners: short note, reason, action needed, and how to opt-out of auto-escalation for bespoke deals.

alex: +1 on opt-out workflow. we should add a `manual_override=true` column that short-circuits playbook.

liam: logging checklist for release: feature flag, backfill id, runbook link, rollback steps, estimated cost. i'll create the release PR once sana posts dry-run output.

marta: perfect. i'm listing owners to ping in the PR: @sana, @alex, @liam. i'll also include the sample CSV and the YAML snippet.

sana: posting results now. small note: ~7% of sampled accounts had partner contacts as primary. we should add a contact role filter to the primary selector.

marta: tracked. i'll add to the playbook review doc. thanks all. :rocket:
